questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
That the place I went to had exciting nature/culture, so you were able to see much new stuff. 
It was also crucial to me that the place I went to was an english speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: just fantastic, unique friendships, and an experience you'll probably never get again.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: you had to do a lot research by yourself. I could have used some more helped when it came to choosing courses at the exchange university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got picked up by a university car when I arrived to the airport, and they drove me to my accommodation. There were also an orientation week for people abroad the week before uni, so you could get a lot of help settling in and with courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in the residential village called Roberts, where you had your own bedroom, but shared bathroom and kitchen. It was also possible to get a studio-room, where you had you own bathroom and kitchen.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: there was a shared kitchen at my accommodation, but there was also a cafe in the residential village, which were selling lunch and dinner to reasonable prices.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: If you live on campus at Monash it is about an hour in public transport from the central city, which is a bit far, but it is by far the best way of meeting new people. You meet a lot of international, exchanges and local students, who you'll live with for a semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The only minus is that the bedrooms are a bit small and the furnitures aren't the best, but it's fine!

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I remember I found it pretty had to see which courses I could take. But in the orientation week they are very helpful, if you wanna change anything.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: not really any help before you arrive to the university, until then you'll have to find out how to yourself.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got the ones I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes time, so don't do it the last minute

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: It was very different from course to course, some were easier than expected and some were harder

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: very different. they have mid semester tests here, and assignments throughout the semester, which counts on your final grade

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to financial accounting
Environmental economics
Statistical machine learning

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Environmental economics were very interesting, especially because you get an insight on how it is in Australia aswell, so you learn a bit about the special nature they have here.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Australia is in general an expensive country.
Alcohol is very expensive, so partying is more expensive than usual.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: More: alcohol, vegables/greens

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can sigh up for almost any sports or social club you want to

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: do all the activities in the orientation week. They are free and is a nice way to see the nature around Melbourne and the city

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I had a weekend trip to Sydney (1,5 hour flight), and went on a roadtrip in the Northern Territory in a campervan from Darwin to Uluru in the Mid-sem break. 
After the exams I went traveling down the east coast from Cairns to Sydney

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: pretty easy, australias culture is not that different

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: just talk to people, they are very nice, and most likely in the same position as you are

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: people coming from all over the world with different backgrounds and stories

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- be openminded
- see as much of the nature around Melbourne (but also australia) as possible
- have fun!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: creating friendships from all over the world

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: it is expensive

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: no

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
